en: The Perfection of Wisdom in One Hundred and Fifty Verses.
Homage, homage to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas!
Homage to the Blessed Noble Perfection of Wisdom!
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was endowed with the various distinctions of the wisdom of the commitment (*samaya*) of the vajra-consecration of all Tathāgatas;
he had attained the consecration of the triple world through the jewel-diadem of all Tathāgatas; he was the great Lord of Yoga of the omniscient wisdom of all Tathāgatas;

he had realized the equality of all mudrās of all Tathāgatas; and by virtue of performing manifold activities, he was the accomplisher of all actions that fulfill every hope of the entire realm of sentient beings without exception.

Mahāvairocana, the eternal Tathāgata who abides in the equality of the three times, the Vajra of all body, speech, and mind, dwelt in the palace of the divine king Sarvakāmadhātūpariparanirmitavaśavartin, which was adorned with the praises and dwellings of all Tathāgatas, inlaid with great precious jewels, beautified by the moon, and graced with various colored bells, wind-stirred silk banners, pennants, garlands, chowries, necklaces, half-necklaces, and strings of pearls.
Together with eight koṭis of bodhisattvas, namely: the bodhisattva mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi and the bodhisattva mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha; and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva Vajramuṣṭi;
and by the bodhisattva mahāsattva Mañjuśrī.
and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sahacittotpāditadharmacakrapravartin, and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Gaganagañja, and with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sarvamārabalapramardin.
AśP 3. Thus, surrounded and honored by eight koṭis of bodhisattvas headed by these, he taught the Dharma;

he proclaimed the holy life (*brahmacarya*) that is virtuous in the beginning, virtuous in the middle, and virtuous in the end, excellent in meaning and excellent in phrasing, unique, complete, pure, and stainless—the gateway to the purification of all phenomena.
AśP 4. That is to say, he taught the method of the perfection of wisdom called "The Gateway to the Purity of the Essential Nature of All Phenomena.
It is as follows: (1) This state of purity of joy is indeed the state of a bodhisattva.
(2) This is the stage of the purification of the arrow of passion, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva;

(3) this is the stage of the purification of the fire of hatred, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva; (4) this is the stage of the purification of the bond of affection, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva.
(5) This is the stage of the purification of sovereign mastery over all dominion, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva.
(6) This is the stage of the purification of views, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva. (7) This is the stage of the purification of delight.
This, namely, the state of a bodhisattva;
(8) this, namely, the state of the purification of craving, is the state of a bodhisattva;
(9) this, namely, the state of the purification of pride, is the state of a bodhisattva.
(10) This is the stage of purity of adornment, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva; (11) this is the stage of purity of gladdening the mind, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva;
(12) this is the stage of purity of illumination, namely, the stage of the bodhisattva.
(13) This is the station of the purity of the body, namely, the station of the bodhisattva;
(14) this is the station of the purity of bodily happiness, namely, the station of the bodhisattva;
(15) this is the station of the purity of form, namely, the station of the bodhisattva.
(16) This is the station of the purity of sound, namely, the station of the bodhisattva; (17) this is the station of the purity of odor, namely, the station of the bodhisattva;
(18) this is the station of the purity of taste, namely, the station of the bodhisattva.
(19) This is the station of the purity of contact, namely, the station of the bodhisattva.
(20) This is the station of the purity of phenomena, namely, the station of the bodhisattva.
For what reason?
For thus all dharmas are pure by nature; through the absence of intrinsic nature in all dharmas, there is the purity of the perfection of wisdom.

Vajrapāṇi, whoever shall hear even once this method of the perfection of wisdom called "The Accomplishment of the Words on the Purity of the Essential Nature of All Dharmas," for them, even though they may accumulate great obscurations of all that is to be known, afflictions, and karma, there shall never be rebirth in the miserable states such as the hells until they reach the seat of awakening.
Furthermore, even the evils committed will go to destruction without suffering.

And whoever shall uphold it, recite it day by day, study it, and attend to it with wise reflection, he shall, in this very life, become a lord of all phenomena through the attainment of the vajra-samādhi of the equality of all phenomena.
He will experience all forms of delight, joy, and gladness;
and in his sixteenth birth as a great bodhisattva, he will attain the state of a Tathāgata and the state of a Vajradhara.
Then the Blessed One— the realization of the Mahāyāna of all Tathāgatas, the embodiment of all maṇḍalas, the supreme being of the entire vajra-realm,

the conqueror of the whole threefold world-system of the triple realm, capable of disciplining the entire realm of sentient beings without exception, the accomplisher of all aims, the Great Vajrapāṇi of all, the Great Samaya surrounded by a retinue of many great secret vajra-beings— [taught] this very meaning of the method of the Perfection of Wisdom.

Illuminating [the world] with a smiling face, holding that primordial great vajra by brandishing it with the left arm while drawing it up to his own heart through yogic application, he entered this *svatattvahṛdaya* (heart-essence of his own reality) called the Great Bliss Vajra Unfailing Samaya: HŪṂ.
Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, again taught this method of the Perfection of Wisdom called "The Manifest Realization of the Vajra-Nature of All Tathāgatas," [stating]:
"Great awakening is the manifest realization of the equality of the vajra, by virtue of its adamantine firmness;
great awakening is the manifest realization of the equality of meaning, by virtue of its single purpose."
The perfect awakening to the equality of all phenomena is great awakening, because of the purity of all phenomena;
the perfect awakening to the equality of everything is great awakening, because of the non-conceptualization regarding the intrinsic nature of all phenomena.

O Vajrapāṇi, whoever shall hear, retain, recite, or cultivate these four dwellings in the Dharma— even if they have practiced all manner of evil— shall transcend all states of woe until reaching the seat of enlightenment,
and shall swiftly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

AśP 9. Then, having spoken this, the Blessed One—holding the Fist of Knowledge (*jñānamuṣṭi*) and illuminating this very word of meaning to a great extent—with a smiling face, spoke this Heart of the Equality of All Dharmas:
*vajra āḥ*.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the subduer of all the wicked, again spoke the production of the perfection of wisdom called "The Compendium of Victory through the Equality of All Dharmas":
"Through the non-proliferation of passion, there is the non-proliferation of hatred;
through the non-proliferation of hatred, there is the non-proliferation of delusion."
Through the non-proliferation of delusion, there is the non-proliferation of all phenomena;
through the non-proliferation of all phenomena, it should be understood that there is the non-proliferation of the perfection of wisdom.

Vajrapāṇi, whoever shall hear, retain, recite, or cultivate this method of the perfection of wisdom, for them there shall be no going to the states of woe, even if they were to cause all sentient beings born within the three realms to fall, provided that this is done under the influence of discipline.
And he will swiftly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

AśP 12. Then Vajrapāṇi, further illuminating this very meaning of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), bound the mudrā called Trilokavijayavajrā. With a frowning brow, a knitted brow, a blazing gaze, a smile, and a face made formidable by slightly bared fangs, standing in the pratyālīḍha posture, he spoke this heart-mantra named Vajrahūṃkāra: VAJRA HŪṂ.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who has attained the dharmatā that is pure by nature, again spoke this meaning of the method of the perfection of wisdom called the "Wisdom-Seal of Avalokiteśvara, the Equality of All Dharmas":
"The purification of all passion in the world leads to the purification of all hatred."
The purification of all stains in the world leads to the purification of all evils;
the purification of all phenomena in the world leads to the purification of all sentient beings;
the purification of all-knowledge in the world leads to the purification of the perfection of wisdom.

Vajrapāṇi, whoever shall hear this method, uphold it, recite it, or cultivate it— even if they remain in the midst of all passion— will not be stained by the adventitious impurities of the faults of passion, just as a lotus is not soiled; and they will swiftly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Then the Blessed One, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, further illuminating this very point of meaning, with a smiling countenance and gazing upon his freedom from the stain of passion and other defilements through the blossoming of a lotus petal, spoke this heart-mantra named *Sarvajagadviśvarūpapadma*: Hrīḥ.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the sovereign of all the three realms, once again [bestowed] the gift of consecration for the sake of the method of the Perfection of Wisdom called the "Womb of Wisdom Arising from the Consecration of All Tathāgatas.
This leads to the attainment of sovereignty over all the three realms;
the gift of wealth leads to the fulfillment of all hopes.
The gift of Dharma leads to the attainment of the equality of all phenomena;
the gift of material things leads to the acquisition of happiness for the entire body, speech, and mind.

Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Ākāśagarbha, with a smiling face, bound upon his own head the garland of the vajra-jewel consecration; further illuminating this very meaning of the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), he spoke this heart-mantra named "The Jewel of the Samaya of All Consecrations": TRĀṂ.

Then the Blessed One— the eternal Tathāgata who has attained the wisdom-mudrās of all Tathāgatas and who holds the fist of all Tathāgatas— once again spoke this *Vajra* named "The Empowerment of the Wisdom-Mudrās of All Tathāgatas" for the sake of the meaning of the method of the Perfection of Wisdom:
"The grasping of the body-mudrā of all Tathāgatas leads to the state of being a Tathāgata."
The grasping of the speech-seal (*vāṅmudrā*) of all Tathāgatas leads to the attainment of all dharmas;
the grasping of the mind-seal (*cittamudrā*) of all Tathāgatas leads to the attainment of all samādhis;
the grasping of the vajra-seal (*vajramudrā*) of all Tathāgatas leads to the supreme accomplishment of the vajra-nature of all body, speech, and mind.

Vajrapāṇi, whoever shall hear this Dharma-discourse, retain it, recite it, explain it, and cultivate it, will obtain all accomplishments, all prosperities, all knowledges, all activities, and the supreme accomplishment of the vajra-nature of all body, speech, and mind.
And he will swiftly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.

Then the Blessed One Vajramuṣṭi, having taken hold of the great samaya-vajra-mudrā and further illuminating this very meaning, with a smiling face, spoke this heart-mantra named "The Samaya of the Accomplishment of All Firm Vajra-mudrās": *Aḥ*.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who is the non-conceptualization of the equality of all phenomena, again spoke this meaning of the method of the perfection of wisdom called the "Chapter on the Syllables of the Wheel":
"All phenomena are empty by virtue of their lack of intrinsic nature;
all phenomena are signless by virtue of their being without signs."
All phenomena are without a basis through the application of non-aspiration;
they are luminous by nature and purified by the perfection of wisdom.
AśP 22–31 is missing;
AśP 32... Then, O Mahāvajreśvara, he attained this heart of reality (*tattvahṛdaya*):
*oṃ vajranetrībhyaḥ svāhā*.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who has reached the ultimate limit of the infinite and boundless, whose dharmas are themselves infinite and without limit, spoke again this meaning of the method of the perfection of wisdom called "The Vajra of the Empowerment of the Ultimate Limit of the Equality of All Dharmas," for the sake of empowering the final consummation of this eon.
Due to the infinity of the perfection of wisdom, there is the infinity of all Tathāgatas;
due to the boundlessness of the perfection of wisdom, there is the boundlessness of all phenomena;
due to the non-duality of the perfection of wisdom, there is the non-duality of all phenomena.
Through the perfection of the perfection of wisdom, there is the non-perfection of all phenomena.
Vajra oṃ, you who are the non-conceptualization of the nature of all phenomena, hili! You who are the merging of the nature of all phenomena, mili! O you who are passionately devoted to all, svāhā!

Vajrapāṇi, whoever shall hear this Dharma-discourse, retain it, recite it, explain it, propagate it, and cultivate it, will— having reached the ultimate stage of the conduct of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas— swiftly attain the state of a Tathāgata or the state of a Vajradhara through the complete perfection of all obscurations.
Homage to all Tathāgatas! Homage to all Vajradharas!
Oṃ, Blessed One, purify from this shore to the further shore! Svāhā!
"Preceded by the syllable Oṃ, I shall effect the crossing of the flood for all sentient beings.
(AśP 35) Then all the Tathāgatas, having assembled, granted their approval to Vajrapāṇi for this Dharma-discourse, so that it might be unfailing and bring swift, unimpeded accomplishment:
"Excellent, excellent, Great Being! Excellent, excellent, Great Bliss!"
Excellent, excellent, Mahāyāna! Excellent, excellent, Mahāmati! (1)
This well-spoken ritual manual, the Vajrasūtra, is empowered by all the Buddhas who hold the vajra; it is the supreme, unfailing discipline. // 2 //
Those who shall uphold this unsurpassed King of Ritual Manuals will be unassailable and invincible against all Māras and their like. (3)
Buddhahood, the state of a bodhisattva, and all supreme accomplishments will be attained before long, just as all the words of the Buddhas declare.
Having spoken this, all the foremost Buddhas together with the Sauraghana deities rejoiced in what was spoken by the Vajra-holder for the sake of the secret accomplishment.

Then the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana, who has attained the secret nature of all Tathāgatas and for whom all phenomena are free from conceptual proliferation, again spoke this supreme, primordial, beginningless, endless, and middle-less gateway to the method of the Perfection of Wisdom— the equality of the Dharma of the Unfailing Vajra— named the Unfailing Vajra Samaya of Great Bliss.
The supreme accomplishment of great passion leads the great bodhisattvas to the supreme accomplishment of great bliss.
The supreme accomplishment of great bliss leads the great bodhisattvas to the supreme accomplishment of the great awakening of all Tathāgatas.
The supreme accomplishment of the great awakening of all Tathāgatas leads the great bodhisattvas to the supreme accomplishment of the complete subduing of all great Māras.
The supreme accomplishment of crushing all the great Māras leads the great bodhisattvas to the supreme accomplishment of sovereignty over the entire triple world.

The supreme accomplishment of mastery over the whole triple world serves as the cause for the great bodhisattvas’ resolute commitment to purifying the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder;

thus, for those great beings of great heroism who are committed until the end of saṃsāra, it leads to the supreme accomplishment of all benefit and happiness for the protection of the realm of sentient beings without exception or remainder.
Oṃ vajra! Oṃ, Mother of all Tathāgatas!
Holder of the Vajra of Great Bliss!
You who enter into the equality of all things!
O you who bring about the destruction of all suffering! O bestower of all happiness! O giver of all happiness! Svāhā!
For what reason?

As long as these excellent sages remain dwelling within the cycle of existence (saṃsāra), they are capable of performing incomparable benefit for sentient beings, remaining unextinguished [in their activity]. // 6 //
Perfumed by the empowerment of the knowledge of skillful means and the perfection of wisdom, they indeed become pure in their very being through the purity of all phenomena. // 7 //

In this world, until the end of existence, those who commit evil always discipline themselves through the subduing of passion and the like; however, for the sake of purifying them, [the Buddhas] themselves discipline [them] until the end of existence. // 8 //
Just as a deep red lotus is not stained by the defects of passion, so those who work for the welfare of the world are never stained by the defects of worldly existence. 9.
But those purified by great passion, possessing great bliss and great wealth, having attained sovereignty over the three realms, firmly act for the benefit of sentient beings. // 10 //
Thus it is said.

O Vajrapāṇi, whoever shall rise every day at dawn and recite or hear this Dharma-discourse, the entrance to the method of the Perfection of Wisdom which is supreme from the beginning, will obtain all happiness and mental well-being, and shall attain in this very life the ultimate accomplishment of the Great Bliss Vajra Unfailing Samaya.
Having attained the supreme siddhi of the secret vajra of all Tathāgatas, he will become a Mahāvajradhara or a Tathāgata.
AśP 40. Then the Blessed One addressed Vajrapāṇi, the lord of the Guhyakas:
"O Lord of the Guhyakas, these twenty-five gateways to the method of the Perfection of Wisdom should be upheld:
Oṃ bodhicittavajre // 1 //"
Oṃ, to the conduct of Samantabhadra! // 2 //
Oṃ Cintāmaṇi. // 3 //
Oṃ, in non-cessation! // 4 //
Oṃ, you who turn back rebirth! // 5 //
Oṃ, to all consciousness! // 6 //
Oṃ, O nature of the Dharma of great dispassion! // 7 //
Oṃ, to the armor of vigor! // 8 //
Oṃ, you who go everywhere! // 9 //
Oṃ, you whose mind is firm in the vajra armor! // 10 //
Oṃ, to all the Tathāgatas! // 11 //
Oṃ, naturally pure! // 12 //
Oṃ, pure through the knowledge of the nature of phenomena! 13.
Oṃ, purifier of karma, hūṃ! // 14 //
Oṃ nisumbhavajriṇi phaṭ! // 15 //
Oṃ, to the passion of desire! // 16 //
Oṃ jaha vajre // 17 //
Oṃ hūṃ, O giver of all! // 18 //
Oṃ hrīḥ. // 19 //
Oṃ, at the mouth of the letter A. // 20 //
Oṃ, to the Perfection of Wisdom. // 21 //
Oṃ aṃ vaṃ hūṃ oṃ aḥ // 22 //
Oṃ, foremost among the bodies of all Tathāgatas! // 23 //
Oṃ, you who are the purity of the speech of all Tathāgatas! // 24 //
Oṃ, vajra of the mind of all Tathāgatas. // 25 //
Vajrapāṇi, this [teaching] will not fall upon the ears of those beings who have not planted roots of merit.
Nor can it be written, read, retained, recited, honored, revered, esteemed, or worshiped by beings who have not planted roots of merit.

On the contrary, those beings who shall hear even a single syllable of this Dharma-discourse, the entrance to the method of the perfection of wisdom, will be those who have planted roots of merit under many Buddhas.

How much more so, Vajrapāṇi, for one who has not honored, revered, esteemed, or worshiped hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of Buddhas, as numerous as the sands of eighty Ganges rivers—by such a person, this entrance to the method of the perfection of wisdom cannot be mastered. What then, if it were complete and fully perfected?
By whomsoever [this] has not been honored, revered, esteemed, or worshiped, by them this entrance to the method of the perfection of wisdom cannot be attained.
This Dharma discourse should be heard.
Therefore, the place on earth where this Dharma discourse circulates will become like a shrine (caitya).
And that person for whom this Dharma discourse has entered their body or is contained in a book will be worthy of veneration for many millions of eons.
He will possess the recollection of his past births for many millions of eons,
and Māra, the Evil One, shall not create any obstacle for him.
Furthermore, the four great kings and other deities shall follow closely behind him to provide protection, defense, and guardianship.
Nor shall he die by failing to avoid dangerous circumstances;
he shall be attended by all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
In brief, in whichever Buddha-field he may desire to be born, there he shall be reborn.
Thus, this Dharma discourse, which is the entrance to the method of the perfection of wisdom, possesses manifold benefits;
moreover, I have proclaimed only a mere fraction of it.
The Blessed One spoke thus.

With joyful minds, the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas headed by Vajrapāṇi, as well as the entire assembly—including the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas—rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
Thus ends the *Bhagavatī Prajñāpāramitā* in one hundred and fifty verses.
